## Overview

Adds the `train-inference-consistency` agent skill under `.agents/skills/` (symlinked from `.claude/skills/`). It guides an agent through making RL training and vLLM rollout produce bitwise identical logprobs (true on-policy RL) while keeping rollout throughput close to the high-performance baseline.

## Claims

- A C0–C10 workflow with explicit pass criteria per gate, from module inventory and proxy model through inference batch / prefill-decode invariance, training forward and backward alignment, two-step RL acceptance, and delivery.
- Guides for the problems that come up on that path: mismatch localization and bisect, training forward and backward validation, which batch-invariant kernel each operator uses and what it costs, quantization conversion chain and QAT, rollout engine behavior (sampling seeds, prefix cache, MTP, R3), performance A/B, exact checkpoint resume, runtime provenance, and paired acceptance.
- The rules come from the DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Nemotron-3.5-Lightning NVFP4 consistency work, where `actor/ppo_kl` and rollout/training logprob diff are 0 at every step.

## Validation

Docs only, no code change.

- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass, including `check-agent-files` (frontmatter, symlink, SKILL.md line budget, every relative link and anchor resolves), `markdownlint-cli2` and `typos`.
- No model evaluation: the change does not affect vLLM behavior.

## Details

- Not a duplicate: no open PR adds a train-inference consistency skill (searched open PRs for "train-inference consistency skill", "batch invariant skill" and `.agents/skills`). `docs/features/batch_invariance.md` documents how to enable batch-invariant inference for users; the skill links to it and covers the training-side alignment and validation process that the docs do not.
- Layout follows `docs/contributing/editing-agent-instructions.md`: `SKILL.md` (31 lines) is the entry point and links to `workflow/`, `guides/` and `practices/`.
- The skill is large (16 files). Each guide is a single file with a symptom table and key rules at the top, so an agent loads only the guide for the problem at hand.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write and translate this skill. The submitter has reviewed the content and is responsible for it.

+Make the training side and the inference side in RL produce bitwise identical logprobs for the same token (diff = 0), and, while keeping 0 diff, bring performance back close to the high-performance baseline.

+# Backward: reuse and validation
+
+## Reusing backward: when you actually need to write your own
+
+When to reuse backward and when to write glue.
+
+### Conclusion
+
+Backward is determined by the **math formula**, not by the forward kernel. The backward of `y = f(x, W)` needs only the formula and the saved inputs: `dX = dY·W`, `dW = dYᵀ·x`. A vLLM forward kernel does not by itself require a new backward. "No backward operator at the same precision" is not a reason to rewrite: under the high_precision contract the backward runs in BF16/FP32 anyway.
+
+### How to wire it: forward once, backward uses what the forward saved
+
+The training forward is the inference forward. Each module is an autograd Function: its forward calls the inference kernel to produce the visible output and saves what its own backward needs (inputs, visible output, LSE, fixed routing IDs, quantized values and scales); its backward uses only those, through a reused library backward or a closed-form VJP. If the inference kernel does not output something the backward needs, change the kernel to output it.
+
+Delivery requires 0 diff and a training step within budget on the main topologies fixed at C1; C6 checks both together. Nemotron audited this against DS4: attention saves q/k/v, out and LSE; routed MoE saves x, the visible FC1 output and the visible output; linear and norms save their inputs; the router saves logits and fixed IDs. Its open gap is Mamba SSD, because vLLM's visible SSD does not output the chunk state.
+
+### Three cases
+
+| Case | Characteristics | Examples | What to do |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| A only rounding differs | Same math; summation order/chunking differs; difference in the last BF16 bit | RMSNorm, Mamba SSD scan, attention, conv1d, unquantized linear | Reuse the training framework's backward (MCore/TE/mamba_ssm); write no code |
+| B forward has rounding | FP8/NVFP4 quantization rounds; the true derivative is 0 almost everywhere | Quantized linear, FP8 Q/K/V | First fix the STE proxy (rounding passes through as 1; dX uses dequantized values by default; DS4 and Nemotron currently approximate with TE high_precision master values, and the deviation must be quantified per [layer 2](#layer-2-gradient-contract-comparison)), then reuse the ordinary BF16 GEMM backward |
+| C no ready-made backward for the whole segment | Composite of several operators with no library backward for the whole segment | Routed experts: sort -> grouped GEMM -> relu² -> restore -> top-k weighted sum | Write glue that chains ready-made operators; GEMM still uses TE grouped GEMM; compare gradients against an independent reference |
+
+Decision flow: (1) does the forward have rounding/quantization (top-k ID selection does not count; IDs are fixed and not differentiated)? No -> A. Yes -> (2) fix the STE contract -> (3) is there a packaged training backward for the whole segment (TE Linear/GroupedLinear, MCore MoE)? Yes -> B, reuse it and feed master values; no -> C, glue. If A has no same-math training implementation, also write only glue. Look first in mLite `primitive/modules` and `ops`, then in MCore/TE/mamba_ssm.
+
+### How DS4 did it
+
+DS4's only hand-written kernel is the small FP8 quantization Triton kernel in the forward. The backward has no hand-written kernel, only PyTorch closed-form formulas and glue, all in FP32.
+
+| Operator | Case | Backward source | What we wrote |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| FP8 dense linear (qkv, shared expert, o-proj) | B | TE `general_gemm`, BF16 master | Nothing |
+| Routed experts (grouped) | B+C | TE `general_grouped_gemm`; reuses gate_up, the output of the forward vLLM FC1, without recomputing | Glue: sort, activation derivative, summation |
+| Sparse attention | A | cuDNN sparse attention backward, consuming the forward's saved out and LSE | Nothing |
+| SwiGLU (with clamp), RMSNorm, q/kv norm, mHC | A | Hand-written closed-form derivative, FP32, `torch.compile` | PyTorch formula |
+| Routing score | A (IDs fixed) | FP32 replay of `sqrt(softplus)` + normalization, handed to autograd | PyTorch formula |
+| Others | A | Generic bridge: forward via vLLM, backward recomputes the PyTorch graph then `autograd.grad` | One utility function |
+
+DS4 wrote its own for four reasons, none of them a missing same-precision backward kernel: (1) library backwards need intermediates from the library's own forward (TE RMSNorm needs rstd, MCore MoE the token permutation; the vLLM forward has neither); (2) model-specific math is not in the library (`sqrt(softplus)` scoring, SwiGLU with clamp, mHC Sinkhorn); (3) discrete selection must copy the forward (recomputed top-k may pick a different expert on ties, so store the IDs and differentiate only the continuous score); (4) the generic bridge costs too much memory and time (autograd stores all 20 mHC iterations; use a closed-form derivative fused with compile). A custom backward function has no autograd graph inside, so its activation derivative must be closed-form (`dynamic_clamped_swiglu_vjp`; likewise relu² in Nemotron `routed_vjp`).
+
+### Three rules when reusing
+
+1. Intermediate definitions must match: attention backward uses the forward's out and LSE, so LSE base (ln or log2), softmax scale and memory layout must line up. If they do not, recompute the forward with the training kernel inside the backward.
+2. Backward need not be bitwise identical: recomputed intermediates differ from the vLLM forward in the last BF16 bit and gradients differ by the same amount, which is allowed. The requirement is that the gradient contract holds and the error is near the noise floor.
+3. Reused code must be verified too, per [layer 1](#layer-1-module-level-vjp-comparison): compare dX and dW against an FP32 reference that does not call the backward under test, with the same dY, in multiples of the noise floor.
+
+### Two test-infrastructure false negatives
+
+- A unit test that instantiated QuantFP8 directly lacked production training's vLLM config context (`CompilationConfig(custom_ops=['none','+quant_fp8'])`, Humming, PP4), and the first long-sequence test failed before computing anything. Fix: the test wrapper uses the production config; production operators and tolerances are unchanged.
+- An import check without GPU visibility makes vLLM select a non-CUDA platform, which cannot import `reshape_and_cache_flash` (exported only on CUDA). Dependency checks need real device visibility.
+- Both are test errors, not train-inference differences.
+
+## Backward validation: is the implementation right, is the approximation reasonable, is training biased
+
+Forward 0 diff shows the logprobs match, not that gradients are right. Validate the backward in three layers:
+
+| Layer | Question answered | Method | Cannot replace |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 1. Module-level VJP comparison | Does the implementation match the agreed gradient contract (missing scale, wrong transpose, broken gradient chain) | compare dX, dW and a one-step update of every module against an independent reference that does not call the backward under test | layers 2 and 3 |
+| 2. Gradient contract comparison | Is the contract reasonable: does an approximation (e.g. dX from the master value) bias training | same batch, compare gradients under the two conventions per class and per layer | layer 1 |
+| 3. Proxy SFT three-arm comparison | Does the whole training chain have a systematic bias | three SFT paths (under test, gradient reference, native baseline) with the same data and hyperparameters | layers 1 and 2 |
+
+Run 1 → 2 → 3. If layer 1 fails, fix the implementation before any SFT. If layer 3 is abnormal, go back to layers 1 and 2. Passing all three clears the backward; none proves long-term RL stability.
+
+### Write down the gradient contract first
+
+#### The three tiers of a weight
+
+In quantized training one parameter has three values, and the gradient must end up at the one the optimizer manages:
+
+| Tier | Precision | What it is |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| main | FP32 | optimizer state; updates accumulate here |
+| master | BF16 | the model parameter, converted from main every step; non-quantized layers compute with it directly |
+| deployed value | NVFP4 / FP8 etc. | master quantized per the deployment rule; both the training forward and inference use these bytes |
+
+Keep the optimizer's parameter identity: when replacing the forward, do not create parameters the optimizer does not know about. The deployed value is not a trainable parameter.
+
+#### Contract table
+
+A kernel without autograd does not need a surrogate gradient: non-quantized GEMM, norm and attention reuse the existing backward when the math matches; STE is needed only through discrete operations such as quantization rounding. Before implementing, decide per module class:
+
+| Item | What must be decided |
+| --- | --- |
+| Visible forward | the inference implementation; input/output dtype, layout; quantize/dequantize positions, scale granularity, rounding, clamp, accumulation precision |
+| Trainable variables | input, master weight, bias, norm, router; whether scale is fixed, stop-gradient or trainable |
+| Surrogate function | whether dX uses the master or dequantized value (see below); identity or clipped STE, and the value at the threshold |
+| Discrete state | fixed expert IDs, sparse indices, ordering; continuous score/combine weights that still need gradients |
+| backward | reused implementation or custom VJP; cast, accumulation/reduction precision, communication and normalization |
+| Save/recompute | quantized values, scale, norm/attention intermediates, routing, RNG; memory cost and recompute rules |
+| Reference and acceptance | independent reference implementation, target shape/execution path, metrics and tolerances agreed in advance |
+
+Identity STE sets the surrogate derivative of Q(x) to 1; clipped STE sets 1 inside the range and 0 outside, with the threshold value stated and never switched silently. Declare weight and activation quantization separately; frozen weights do not mean nothing upstream of the activations needs gradients.
+
+#### Linear: which weight dX uses
+
+For `Y = X · Wᵀ + b` with upstream gradient `G`:
+
+```text
+dW = Gᵀ · X_ref        # returns to master via STE, then the optimizer updates main
+db = sum_over_tokens(G)
+dX = G · W_ref
+```
+
+Two choices for `W_ref`:
+
+- **Dequantized value**: `W_ref = dequant(quant(W_master))`, the value the forward actually used. This is the true derivative of `Y = X · Wqᵀ` with respect to X, and what fake-quant QAT gets from autograd. **Use this by default.**
+- **Master value**: `W_ref = W_master` (BF16). Reuses the plain BF16 GEMM backward without dequantizing; the cheapest hookup when the inference kernel takes only packed bytes and has no backward. Cost: dX is no longer the exact forward derivative and ignores the quantization error's effect on the input gradient.
+
+The two give different gradients and must not be swapped silently. With the master value, the layer-2 comparison is mandatory: quantify and record the bias. Likewise for activation quantization, state whether `X_ref` is the quantized or original activation.
+
+Before reusing a linear or grouped GEMM backward, check flatten/transpose, padding and valid tokens, bias reduction, saved inputs, scaling and the accumulation/backprop dtype. Matching output shape does not prove reusability.
+
+### Layer 1: module-level VJP comparison
+
+#### How to build the reference implementation
+
+The reference may use PyTorch ops and autograd but **must not call the backward under test**, or both paths share the error. For discrete operations implement the agreed surrogate backward explicitly; the zero gradient of bare rounding is not a reference.
+
+This bridge takes the output value from the inference implementation and the gradient from an independent surrogate. Use it to build the reference path:
+
+```python
+import torch
+
+
+class VisibleWithSurrogate(torch.autograd.Function):
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, visible, surrogate):
+        assert visible.shape == surrogate.shape
+        assert visible.device == surrogate.device
+        assert visible.dtype == surrogate.dtype
+        return visible
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
+        return None, grad_output
+
+
+with torch.no_grad():
+    visible = inference_linear(x, deployment_weight, scales)
+w_ref = dequantize(deployment_weight, scales)  # default contract; use master_weight for the master-value contract
+surrogate = torch.nn.functional.linear(x, w_ref, bias)
+y = VisibleWithSurrogate.apply(visible.detach(), surrogate)
+```
+
+- Build the surrogate graph in normal grad mode, outside the custom Function's forward.
+- With the dequantized surrogate, `w_ref`'s gradient must reach master via STE: bridge a tensor valued as the dequantized weight whose gradient passes straight to master, then feed it to a plain linear.
+- Do not use `visible + surrogate - surrogate.detach()`: floating-point add/subtract and compiler transforms change the result. Do not modify the bridge output in place downstream.
+- This bridge is the independent validation reference, not the production wiring; production wiring is in [How to wire it](#how-to-wire-it-forward-once-backward-uses-what-the-forward-saved).
+- `visible_forward(visible, native, *inputs)` is another way to write the same bridge: `visible` saves inputs without building a graph, `native` is the training framework's implementation of the same math and reruns the forward on those inputs in backward; precision and speed depend on which `native` is chosen.
+
+#### Comparison steps
+
+1. **Fix the state.** Fix inputs, weights, quantization config, mask/routing. Reference and candidate get independent copies; clear accumulated gradients. Check that the visible forward matches inference, then the saved state the backward needs; at integration, confirm the real forward produces that state.
+2. **Same upstream gradient.** Both sides use the same external dY, dtype and values. Cover fixed random, zero, and sparse (non-zero at selected positions) gradients, then samples from real training. `y.sum().backward()` alone misses transpose, permutation and broadcast errors.
+3. **Compare item by item.** Compare dX, dW and every bias/norm/router/scale gradient separately: missing, shape, finiteness, non-zero where expected. Do not ignore unused differentiable inputs by default; list parameters the branch genuinely does not use. Report max absolute error, relative L2 `‖g − g_ref‖₂ / max(‖g_ref‖₂, eps)`, norm ratio and cosine; direction alone is not enough. With a zero norm the cosine is undefined; use absolute error.
+4. **Set tolerances in advance.** Derive atol/rtol and the relative L2 threshold from dtype, reduction length and reference precision; record the reasoning. No single threshold for all modules, no relaxing after a failure, and no relaxing a same-semantics kernel optimization because "STE is an approximation anyway". Cross-framework bitwise identity is not required.
+5. **Coverage.** Small M (decode), large M (training/prefill), different context lengths, unaligned tails, padding/packing/mask, zeros and extreme values; both sides of the quantization threshold, the saturation region, different scales. For MoE cover empty experts, repeated routing, shared experts, top-k ties; for shared parameters check gradient accumulation across use sites. Test under the target dtype/layout, recompute, autocast, CUDA Graph, gradient accumulation and the actual parallel reduction; local first, then integrated.
+6. **One-step update.** From the same parameters and optimizer state, run one update each and compare the change in master. If gradients are close but updates differ, check scaling, clipping, optimizer state and parameter binding.
+
+Cross-check smooth non-quantized modules with small, high-precision [gradcheck](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.gradcheck.html) or finite differences: fix the discrete branch, avoid non-smooth boundaries, and perturb the weights the forward actually sees. **Do not validate STE with finite differences of the real quantized forward**: that measures the discrete forward, which the STE surrogate derivative deliberately differs from.
+
+#### What to check per module
+
+| Module | Reuse first | Semantics to check |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Dense/QKV/LM head | training linear/grouped VJP, gradient returns to master | dX value convention, cast, bias, gradient accumulation of shared parameters |
+| Norm/RoPE | existing training VJP, FP32 statistics if needed | epsilon, RMS or LayerNorm, position offset, rotation layout |
+| Activation + quantization | the actual composition of activation derivative and STE | saturation region, whether scale is detached, fusion order |
+| Attention/sparse attention | training backward with the same mask/index semantics | causal boundary, softmax scale, LSE definition, GQA, order of selected KV; do not mix auxiliary quantities from different forwards |
+| MoE | expert linear/grouped VJP and a differentiable combine | inverse dispatch permutation, gradient accumulation of repeated tokens, empty experts, shared experts, top-k weight normalization |
+| Router/sparse selection | fix the discrete selection, keep the continuous score's derivative | no continuous gradient for IDs/indices; do not detach the whole router output |
+| Linear attention/SSM | training backward with the same chunked arithmetic | chunk boundary, initial state, state precision, conv state |
+| Selected logprob | log-softmax/gather VJP matching the definition | vocab-shard reduction, temperature, token mask, loss normalization |
+
+Recompute must save or deterministically rebuild the scale, routing/indices, RNG and necessary intermediates, and must not switch the surrogate function.
+
+### Layer 2: gradient contract comparison
+
+Layer 1 answers "does the implementation equal the contract", not "is the contract reasonable". When the contract contains an approximation (most often dX from the master instead of the dequantized value), quantify its distance from the exact derivative:
+
+1. On a fixed checkpoint and batch, compute dX (and gradients related to activation quantization) for every quantized layer under both conventions.
+2. Report cosine and norm ratio per module class and per layer; inspect outlier layers.
+3. Measure each target precision combination separately: changing weight or activation precision changes the bias.
+
+On Nemotron-H (NVFP4 routed experts, FP8 Mamba projections), master-value and dequantized-value dX have cosine ≈0.99 and norm ratio ≈1.00 per class and layer, with both BF16 and FP8 activations, so this approximation does not cause the training score gap. Remeasure for other precisions, a larger learning rate or longer training.
+
+### Layer 3: Proxy SFT three-arm comparison
+
+After the first two layers pass, run a controlled SFT over the whole training chain:
+
+| Path | Visible forward | backward | Purpose |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Under test | aligned inference numerics | production backward | the scheme to deliver |
+| Gradient reference | same as under test at the same parameter snapshot | independent surrogate reference (the bridge above works) | isolate backward implementation errors |
+| Native baseline | original training numerical path | verified original training backward | measure the recipe's overall quality change |
+
+- First compare gradients and one-step update of under-test vs gradient-reference on a fixed checkpoint and batch, then run curves; once trajectories diverge, visible values differ too. The under-test vs native-baseline gap includes quantization and forward-path differences, not only backward. If the gradient reference's full curve is unaffordable, compare on representative batches and state the missing range.
+- Controlled variables: initial weights and optimizer state, data and order, labels/mask, packing, loss normalization, global batch and gradient accumulation, learning rate and schedule, clipping, precision and loss scaling, seed, recompute policy.
+- Record train loss, fixed-validation-set NLL, gradient norm, update RMS, clipping ratio, non-finite values, throughput, against optimizer step or cumulative effective tokens. Fix the comparison window and acceptable deviation before the run; a short run is only a smoke test.
+- Localization: loss differs at the initial weights -> check forward, data, mask; initial loss matches but one-step update differs -> backward, reduction, scale, clipping, optimizer; diverges only after several steps -> save the first abnormal checkpoint, check recompute, quantization refresh, learning rate, RNG, then replay at the same weights.
+- Mark unexplained or unbudgeted differences inconclusive; do not cover them with forward 0 diff.
+
+On Nemotron-H the three paths (aligned trainer with BF16 activations, Megatron QAT, Megatron BF16) ran 40 steps on gsm8k with the same data in the same order: loss 0.3388 / 0.3383 / 0.3374, gradient norm 0.685 / 0.674 / 0.728, curves overlapping. The training loop itself is fine; the RL score gap comes from RL-specific factors.
+
+### Common false differences
+

+- **pinned memory:** page-locked host memory for direct GPU DMA (`cudaHostAlloc` / `cudaHostRegister`), cached by PyTorch's caching host allocator.
+- **cgroup:** limit `memory.max`, usage `memory.current`, split in `memory.stat` into anon, file (page cache) and shmem.
+- **RSS and PSS:** RSS counts shared pages fully in every process; PSS splits them, so only summed PSS approximates the physical total.
+- **DCP / Megatron dist_ckpt:** PyTorch and Megatron distributed checkpoint formats; each rank writes its shard, `.metadata` last.
+- **staging / D2H:** the host buffer GPU tensors are copied into before writing to disk.
+- **Ray object store (plasma):** Ray's shared memory for passing objects, mapped into each worker and charged via PSS.
+- **old-logprob:** the logprob training recomputes for rollout tokens with the pre-update policy.
+- **Ray OOM threshold:** `RAY_memory_usage_threshold`, the usage fraction at which Ray kills workers. Default 0.95.

+- Check file, memory and derived state separately; complete files can still mismatch on the first step after restore.

+- Completion marker last; clear the old directory before overwriting; all ranks check and fail together; a missing file raises instead of falling back to a fresh optimizer.

+- Set rollout `gpu_memory_utilization` per training mode ([5](#5-gpu-memory-set-gpu_memory_utilization-per-mode-when-training-and-rollout-are-colocated)).
+- Save fixes pass [the acceptance in 3.2](#32-reproduce-and-discriminate). Before a long run on a new save path or layout, run to the first save and do one kill→resume.
+- Resume is proven by matching per-rank digests in a new process, a byte-identical first export, an aligned first old-logprob and one non-zero update; `resume_mode=auto` alone proves nothing.
+- Read host memory as anon/file/shmem; `memory.current` includes page cache, and Ray kills on it.

+| Rule | If you do not |
+| --- | --- |

+Host memory fails in two ways in long RL runs: phase **peaks** (save / load / sleep) hitting the limit, and slow per-step **growth**; they are measured differently (1-4). +| Source | Mechanism |
+| --- | --- |
+| Pinned buffer of optimizer offload | The caching host allocator rounds up to a power of 2, so the footprint is tens of percent above the nominal state; summed across ranks it pushes residency before save close to the limit |
+| Parameter shards of FSDP CPU offload | Each rank's shard stays resident on CPU; doubles if load creates a second pinned copy |
+| D2H staging during save | Stays in the pinned cache pool; whether `torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache()` releases it must be verified per save path |
+| CPU backup of serving sleep | L1 sleep keeps one full backup per rank; the pinned cache is not returned after wake |
+| Ray object store | plasma mappings count into each process's PSS as shared pages; node shmem does not grow with it (3) |

+A floating-point difference may vanish in later rounding, masking or routing, so "this layer differs" is not monotonic in depth and O(log L) does not always find the first difference. +After isolating the side ([01](#isolate-the-side-first)) and bisecting ([02](#bisect-and-first-divergence)), classify the difference, then decide what to touch. Precision comes last. Model-specific probes, runtime patches and measurements stay in the model working directory.

+### Classification table
+
+| Class | Evidence | Handling |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Correctness error | Missing weights, wrong mask/position/layout, wrong scale/block, wrong quantization range, operator semantics violate the contract | Must be fixed and the original failing path re-verified; for a diagnostic task, deliver the reproducer and evidence first, without widening modify permission |
+| Normal floating-point difference | Explained by same-version repeatability/reduction/kernel noise, no contract error found | Report the noise floor and task impact; bit-exact is not the only pass condition |
+| Error from correct quantization | Mapping and quantization rules are correct, and a same-input control localizes the divergence to the quantization path | Precision ablation in the order below |
+| Unlocalized | Insufficient evidence or confounded variables | Keep unknown, continue with minimal probes, do not declare "it is just quantization" |

+Precision ablation order: supported and affordable high-precision rollout → QAT matching the serving rules → real low-precision training (most backend requirements, last). +Keep a single checkpoint source; open a separate high-precision adapter branch when needed.

+### Handling order
+
+Input mismatch → weight mismatch → discrete path mismatch (top-k, index) → kernel numerics → precision contract. Rule out each item before moving to the next.

Set tolerances from the model and the baseline; do not copy another model's 0.002. Statistics on a fixed old trajectory are diagnostics, not a KL estimate of the current policy.

+def compare_logprobs(a, b):

+    n = bad = 0; first = None; max_err = 0.0
+    for uid in sorted(a):
+        (x, mx), (y, my) = a[uid], b[uid]
+        assert torch.equal(mx, my), f"{uid}: masks differ"
+        x, y = x[mx], y[my]
+        ix = x.view(torch.int16 if x.dtype == torch.bfloat16 else torch.int32)
+        iy = y.view(torch.int16 if y.dtype == torch.bfloat16 else torch.int32)
+        diff = (ix != iy).nonzero()

+## Key rules

+1. "NVFP4/FP8" is only a format name; a different block scale selection, global scale convention, rounding or static/dynamic activation gives different bytes. Inventory the checkpoint's full rules first.
+2. Use the rules of a mainstream implementation (TE, ModelOpt, NeMo-RL) that matches the checkpoint; do not invent your own. Verify from the real BF16 release, not from dequantized weights.

+4. Compute scale on the full logical tensor. A fusion group shares scale (VERL NVFP4: QKV, gate/up fused global scale). Quantizing each shard separately and concatenating is forbidden.

+Same dtype is not same computation, and QAT is not bit-exact. +Adding vLLM's static FP8 activation fake-quant to training aligns single-layer output to the BF16 noise floor, but end-to-end probs_diff gets about 10% worse: FP8 rounding is discontinuous, so any element-wise upstream mismatch flips codes and amplifies the difference. To judge, add relative noise δ only to the training-side input and sweep the output error; the crossover was about δ≈1%, and activation quantization hurts when upstream mismatch exceeds it. +### 6. Why QAT does not train
+
+Train-inference consistency is the strictest QAT: forward uses quantized weights, the high-precision master accumulates updates, STE passes the gradient back. In W4A16 (the FP4 code is decoded to BF16 in a register and goes through the BF16 tensor core; the gain is 1/4 the weight bandwidth), W4A4 and W8A8 alike, the computed values are "code × scale".

+#### 6.1 Dead zone

+- Each NVFP4 element has only 8 values, 0/0.5/1/1.5/2/3/4/6 × scale, with RNE rounding. From a dequantized checkpoint the master sits on grid points, half a spacing from every decision boundary, and must travel that half spacing before the code changes.
+- At lr 1e-6 one step moves the master about 0.01%; a few hundred steps move it far less than half a spacing, so deployed values stay byte-for-byte unchanged. RL gradients are more random than SFT, closer to a random walk, and need more steps.
+- Result: NVFP4-covered parameters (on Nemotron-H, routed/shared experts and lm_head, the bulk) have zero deployed change, and validation NLL is clearly worse than the native BF16 baseline; freezing these weights explains about half the gap.
+- Recomputing block scale does not flip codes earlier: from grid points requant is idempotent, the E4M3 scale only changes code after block amax moves 3-6%, and a tiny global scale change only rescales the whole tensor.
+- Mainstream QAT (NeMo-RL QARL, slime/Kimi INT4, Jet-RL) starts from the original BF16 weights, which lie between grid points, so any small drift flips a proportional share of codes and there is no dead zone. INT4 with 1×32 groups from a dequantized checkpoint stalls the same way.
+- FP8 is barely affected: floating-point relative spacing is 6-12%, small elements have small absolute spacing, and some elements are always near a boundary. DS4 also starts from dequantized FP8 and is affected only mildly.
+
+#### 6.2 Fix
+
+Preferred: use the original BF16 weights (the real BF16 release) as the master and requantize every step by the same rule (Nemotron-H: TE 4over6, E4M3 upper bound 256). State two points:
+
+- **θ0 is not equal to the official checkpoint bytes.** Requantizing from the real BF16 release, 99.776% of Nemotron-H's NVFP4 bytes are identical and 24 of 46 FP8 tensors (ModelOpt calibrated scale) differ. Proxy SFT gives the cost: 300-step val NLL A-bf16 3.4685 vs C-dequant 3.4641 / C-bf16 3.4373, about 0.03 nat, present at θ0 and not growing during training. This policy needs human confirmation.
+- **Three acceptance items** (all pass on Nemotron-H): (1) with zero updates, re-exported bytes equal θ0 (not the official checkpoint); (2) fast-tier RL θ0/θ1/θ2 is 0 diff and deployed bytes start changing; (3) proxy SFT gap to the native BF16 baseline is within budget.
+
+Alternative, keeping θ0 bytes: add a fixed small jitter to move the master off grid points (toward the neighboring cell, at most half a step; after requant check per block that bytes are unchanged, and roll back changed blocks). Not recommended: stochastic-rounding requantization (about 1.4× deployment error, needs a self-written quantizer, no mainstream precedent), raising lr (under Adam equivalent to QuRL UAQ, only shortens the dead zone, 10× lr is outside the usual RL range), and frozen base + LoRA (QeRL, gives up full-parameter updates). Whichever you choose, state that from a dequantized checkpoint at lr 1e-6, NVFP4 deployed values do not change for roughly the first 10³-10⁴ steps. See [P24](#p24-master-starts-on-the-quantization-grid).

+- Symptom: packed weights concatenated after an FSDP/TP sharded export differ from quantizing the full tensor.

+- Symptom: wrong values after serving fuses gate/up, or the exporter reports a missing pair.

+# Recipe, evaluation and paired acceptance
+
+Which recipe items must match the reference implementation mathematically (not by name), what puts two evaluations on the same measurement basis, and how to pair two arms so a conclusion can be drawn. The reference recipe for train-inference consistency is [verl#7688](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7688) (DS4 exact 0-diff true on-policy). Which reference a model aligned with, and the values it ended up using, are per-model facts and are not recorded here.
+
+## Find by question
+
+| Question | Where to go |
+| --- | --- |
+| Does a 5% gap between two arms count as a gap | [Paired acceptance](#paired-acceptance): noise floor, median over multiple pairs, confounders |
+| The validation score only takes a few discrete values | [Evaluation contract](#evaluation-contract): under greedy the score is a multiple of 1/number of problems |
+| How to design the BI=0 baseline arm | [How the two arms are defined](#how-the-two-arms-are-defined) |
+
+## Key rules
+
+1. Align the math, not the names; read the final CLI/resolved config, not the README or the model name.
+2. Tabulate every deviation from the reference: item, reference value, our value, why, which conclusion it affects.
+3. One recipe, one image, a switch selects the arm (following DS4 `EXACT_ALIGNMENT`, default BI=1; BI=0 goes through Bridge/mcore + R3 + QAT); deviations live only in the switch.
+4. If any of the six evaluation items differs, it is not the same score: dataset version, prompt template, sampling parameters, number of repeats, scorer, length cap.
+5. Rising training reward, probs_diff of 0, and a held-out score gain are three separate conclusions; none substitutes for another.
+6. Before running, fix what is compared, how it is computed, the pass line and the noise floor; plant a known error to confirm the criterion can return FAIL.
+7. One artifact answers one question: run and report performance, quality and consistency separately.
+8. List confounders first, then compare; each is either aligned or quantified separately ([paired acceptance](#paired-acceptance)).
+9. Keep failure records as they are and append new results; keep reruns and changed questions apart.

+## One recipe, one image: deliver true on-policy and the regular baseline with the BI switch
+
+Following DS4's EXACT_ALIGNMENT: one delivery image, one recipe, and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, defined by the recipe, selects the whole arm. +# Rollout engine and sampling
+
+In RL the rollout engine (vLLM) pauses, sleeps and wakes next to the training process, its sampling randomness must be auditable, prefix cache and speculative decoding affect whether the same token sequence is bitwise identical, and RL-only features such as R3 constrain the engine config. Section 6 is a debugging procedure: save one rollout and replay the old-logprob forward. Measurement bases and A/B methods are in [Performance and profiling](performance.md); BI kernels and cudagraph are in [BI kernels](bi-kernels.md).
+
+## 1. Sampling seed collision
+
+**Mechanism.** Each vLLM DP engine resets the global RNG with the same `seed` at the end of warmup. Requests without a seed sample from the global stream, so the n-th request samples the same tokens on every engine. When GRPO spreads the siblings of one prompt across DP engines, many samples in a group repeat: before the fix, Nemotron had only 64-70 distinct responses out of 256 and up to 43% of sibling pairs identical; after the fix, 256/256. The fraction of zero-advantage groups barely changes with the fix; zero advantage mostly comes from task difficulty, not seed collision.
+
+**Fix.** Reset the global RNG by `(seed, data_parallel_index)`; index 0 is bitwise identical to the old behavior (vllm-project/vllm#59788, merged). Use `data_parallel_index`, not `data_parallel_rank`: dense (non-MoE) models run independent engines under DP, and `reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()` resets `data_parallel_rank` to 0 (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py`), so 4 engines get the same seed stream and n=4 gets worse. Nemotron is MoE and goes through `DPEngineCoreProc` with a correct rank, so its 1024/1024 verification on verl holds, but only the index version fixes dense models.
+
+**How to accept.** In the rollout dump, count distinct samples per group and the fraction of fully identical sibling pairs. With different seeds the baseline is about 0.1% identical sibling pairs, all short answers of <=8 tokens (the model outputs `\boxed{}` directly), and about 1-3% share a prefix of >=16 tokens. Anything above this is RNG correlation.
+
+**Do not do this.** verl `rollout.full_determinism=True` gives the n responses in a group the same seed. Do not enable it.
+
+**Greedy cannot verify the fix.** Under greedy, n repeats are identical (Nemotron: 32 of 32), and the score is a multiple of 1/number of problems (AIME with 30 problems: multiples of 1/30; 13/30 -> 19-22/30). A greedy A/B before and after the seed fix shows no difference because greedy does not sample. Rising entropy and the three config curves overlapping are visible only on sampling runs.
+
+## 2. Prefix cache semantics
+
+**Premise.** "Enabling PC does not change the numerics" requires the same request to be bitwise identical on hit, miss, and PC off. For pure attention models KV block reuse guarantees this. For stateful layers (Mamba2 conv/ssm state) it depends on which states the engine copies.
+
+**The Mamba2 pitfall.** vLLM's Mamba align mode copies only the conv and ssm states. Under BI=1, Mamba2 uses exact replay (ported from vllm#55905, which stores three extra chunk buffers x/dt/B) and needs 5 states, so BI=1 Mamba2 originally rejected PC. The fix copies every state in each layer's declared state list; after that, hit/miss/PC off are bitwise identical. Early versions had a convolution window alignment bug in state export (written aligned to the tail, read from the head).
+
+**Cost.** PC under BI=0 has a measurable cost: in Mamba align mode each decode step adds a batch of eager launches, and an 8K prefill is split into two segments. The approach in upstream #58851 is the best.
+
+**Confounders between the two arms.** BI=1 Mamba2 rejects PC while the BI=0 R3 AuxOutput forces PC on, so PC on/off is a confounder in the BI=0 vs BI=1 throughput comparison. List confounders first, then compare; see [paired acceptance](recipe-and-acceptance.md#paired-acceptance).
+
+**Relation to cudagraph.** A PC hit changes the token count of a step. Piecewise cudagraph chooses between the graph and eager fallback by total token count vs `max_cudagraph_capture_size`. Each path is batch-invariant on its own, but the two are not bitwise equal. Under BI, pin `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`; see [BI kernels](bi-kernels.md).
+
+**Checks for stateful layers and caches.** Mamba/SSM must also save chunk boundary state and partial input buffers; check aligned/unaligned split, cross-chunk and restore separately. Cover indexing and capacity of long-context KV/page/workspace near the boundaries.
+
+When testing prefill, confirm whether the prefix cache was hit; during diagnosis, disable or isolate it if needed so the target path executes. Verify the production cache's hit, reuse, and preemption/recompute paths separately. Do not make a comparison pass by clearing the cache and then claim the original lifecycle is fixed.
+
+For performance fixes on the cache path, use bitwise equality with "cache off" as the gold standard: hit positions outside chunk boundaries, every DP rank, recomputed hits after forced preemption, and chunks truncated by the scheduling budget; confirm in the trace that the target branch executed. Then add a hook that checks the device-side state index against the host prediction at every step, plus a per-problem quality evaluation. Two fixes that each pass alone may silently break when stacked; the combination must pass the gate on its own.
+
+## 3. MTP / speculative decoding
+
+- The Nemotron checkpoint has `num_nextn_predict_layers: 1`, and the MTP block is not quantized (bf16). It does not take part in training; the training side must explicitly skip its mapping ([training forward](training-forward.md)).
+- Usable with BI=0. BI=1 + MTP requires the logprob from speculative verification to be bitwise identical to the full forward; without verifying this you cannot claim true on-policy.
+- If used, use it in both arms; otherwise neither the throughput nor the logprob comparison holds.
+
+## 4. R3 (routed experts replay) feature constraints
+
+- **What is returned.** One `(num_moe_layers, top_k)` row of uint8 routed expert ids per token (Nemotron: 52 layers x 6 = 312 B), returned to the trainer with the request's CompletionOutput for route replay. 0 is a valid expert id; check distinctness, not non-zero.
+- **PC must be on.** The R3 AuxOutput is keyed by KV block hash; with PC off there is no key. This is why the BI=0 arm in §2 is forced to enable PC; the keys-only form (PR 57968) does not lift it.
+- **Why per-step return is expensive.** 312 B exceeds the 256 B msgpack zero-copy threshold, so each request's row per step becomes a separate frame, and the frontend accumulates millions of small objects per request before concatenating them at the end. The overhead is on the engine->frontend return path, not in the capture hook. The fix returns once at request finish (finish-only) and packs each step into one ndarray on worker->engine. `output_processor` already exposed `routed_experts` only at finish, so semantics are unchanged.
+- **There is another floor below R3.** msgpack unpacking of three small ndarrays per token for sampling logprobs is a fixed frontend cost (about 25-30 µs/token), larger than everything else left after R3 is fixed. BI=1 does not see it when the engine is the bottleneck; BI=0 has a faster engine and hits it. Two arms tying on e2e is often due to this, not the kernel. Check the frontend asyncio busy fraction before comparing the arms ([Performance and profiling](performance.md)).
+- **What does not change.** R3 adds no GPU->CPU sync, async scheduling is kept, capture writes into a statically preallocated buffer, and cudagraph is unaffected. flashinfer_cutedsl and Humming are both modular MoE (they receive the router's top-k), so moving R3 into the kernel saves nothing.
+- **Limits of the equivalence check.** BI=1 cannot run the equivalence check (Mamba2 BI rejects PC while AuxOutput forces PC, until the §2 fix lands). BI=0 compares sha with strictly serial single-request greedy, but BI=0 routing is itself not batch-invariant, and an unpatched baseline also repeatedly shows partial inequality against the same reference. So first measure the drift with several baseline-vs-baseline runs; the patch counts as equivalent only if it fully equals one clean reference. Bitwise comparison of concurrent greedy dumps is not evidence.
+
+## 5. Lifecycle and GPU memory ledger
+
+**Three pause modes** (`EngineCore.pause_scheduler`): `abort` marks all running requests `FINISHED_ABORTED`, queues new requests, and optionally clears the cache; `wait` queues new requests but keeps stepping until running requests finish (not supported by the inproc engine); `keep` pauses everything, and the Future completes when the output queue is empty. In all three modes the Future returned by pause is the barrier; until it completes, workers still step. In `abort` mode the client receives aborted outputs and must resend them. Requests that arrive during pause are queued and released at resume, using the **new** weights. These are "orphan requests" (pause issued before the rollout tail finishes, or the agent loop sending during pause), and their tokens belong to no single policy version. Before each step's pause, confirm in-flight is 0; after resume, confirm the queue is empty. The HTTP endpoints `/sleep`, `/wake_up`, `/is_sleeping` and pause/resume are dev endpoints and need `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`, otherwise 404.
+
+**Three sleep levels** (`EngineCore.sleep`, `Worker.sleep`):
+
+| level | What it does | GPU memory | Host memory |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 0 | Only pauses scheduling | Unchanged | Unchanged |
+| 1 | Offloads weights to CPU, drops the KV cache, clears the prefix cache | Frees KV and weights | One weight backup per rank (DS4.1 78.61 GiB); the pinned cache is not returned after wake, see [Checkpoint and resume](checkpoint-resume.md) |
+| 2 | Discards all GPU memory, saves only `named_buffers` to CPU | All freed | Small |

+After L2, `wake(weights)` only reallocates GPU memory; the contents are uninitialized. "Reserved is very high but still no GPU memory" after wake is an allocator boundary problem: PyTorch's reserved-but-unallocated blocks cannot be used by another allocation path such as CuMem; see [Checkpoint and resume](checkpoint-resume.md#3-reserved-is-high-so-why-can-wake-still-have-no-gpu-memory).
+
+**Set gpu_memory_utilization by training mode.** The training process does not fully release GPU memory during rollout. Write the value into the recipe per training mode; check the resolved value inside the container and the KV budget in the vLLM log, not the outer setting. Measured values and rules per mode are in [Checkpoint and resume](checkpoint-resume.md#5-gpu-memory-set-gpu_memory_utilization-per-mode-when-training-and-rollout-are-colocated).
+
+**Metrics are cumulative.** `vllm:*_total` counts since process start; when one engine runs several phases, always use `after − before`. Why the first phase happens to be right and how to cross-check are in [Performance and profiling](performance.md#metrics-are-cumulative-values).
+
+**DP traffic lands on rank 0.** When the Rust frontend sends one request at a time, all of them land on rank 0 (engine selection is `min_by_key(routing_score)`, which takes the first on equal load). "No events on rank 1" then means no traffic, not broken routing. Use `X-data-parallel-rank` to pin requests to each rank in turn. The two frontends interpret this header differently: Python in hybrid mode validates it as a local index in `[0, dp_local_size)`, Rust uses the global rank; do not send it to a single-rank service. Python hybrid/external LB with a dense model does not start (`DPAsyncMPClient` asserts `stats_update_address`, upstream #32252); test Python hybrid with an MoE model.
+

+
+## 6. Save one rollout and replay the old-logprob forward
+
+### When to use
+
+For a difference that shows up once across many RL steps, save the failing input batch and matching policy early. Rerunning the rollout changes tokens, scheduling, lengths, cache, packing and later training data at once, hiding whether an intervention worked.
+
+1. Save the framework batch and the policy identity after the real rollout ends and before the old-logprob forward; append the trainer scores after the comparison.
+2. Verify that the save hook executed, that sequence / valid token counts match the log, and that the data reads back.
+3. Use the framework's existing training-only/repeat entry point to read the same batch; restore its weights.

+5. Run A/A first, then change one layout factor. If A/A itself is unstable, first check randomness, mutable buffers, async streams and runtime state.
+
+### Minimal matrix

+| Variant | Change | Answers |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| A | Original packing | Can the frozen input reproduce it |
+| B | Exact repeat of A | Is it run-to-run nondeterministic |

+| E | Separate process or equivalent node | Does it depend on initialization/device state |

+# Training-side model support
+
+How to build a training implementation cheaply and prove it computes the same math as inference. Where training weights come from (master -> training forward weights) is in [Precision, quantization and QAT](precision-quant.md).
+
+## Three routes
+
+The routes differ in where parallelism and kernels come from. In all three we write the model.
+
+| | MCore (Megatron-Bridge) | FSDP2 (VERL's HF interface path) | mLite |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Positioning | Mature TP/PP/EP/CP, main production RL path | Cheapest: write only the model, no parallelism | Built for consistency: forward calls vLLM kernels, backward reuses the training implementation |
+| Forward source | MCore kernels (TE, grouped GEMM) | Our PyTorch model to vLLM semantics, in the Transformers `PreTrainedModel` interface for the VERL loader and PEFT | vLLM kernels (`visible_forward(visible, native, ...)`) |
+| Achievable consistency | BI=0, via R3 + importance sampling | BI=0 | BI=1, logprob raw bytes identical |
+| What to write for a new model | Bridge weight mapping + modules MCore lacks (Mamba/SSM, special norms) | Whole model: config class, checkpoint loading (with dequantization), per-layer forward, per-operator precision contract; autograd backward, filled in where missing | One `model/<name>/`: config, checkpoint mapping, assembly, protocol; modules from `primitive/modules` |
+| Typical pitfalls | Mapping checks values, not semantics; MCore and vLLM math differ (MoE activation clamp) | bf16 autocast around the VERL forward rewrites module precision; `--system-site-packages` ABI; PyTorch reference (Mamba scan) too slow; loading a third-party implementation from the image by mistake | Private modules inside the model directory, bypassing the shared skeleton |
+
+Choose after the [module inventory](#module-inventory-and-placement-rules), by: is BI=1 needed, how many backwards are missing, what parallelism is needed. Nemotron looked cheap by name; FA4, Mamba scan and W4A16 MoE all lacked a backward.
+
+## Find by symptom
+
+| Symptom / question | Where to go |
+| --- | --- |
+| New model loads and config parses, but unclear whether it can train | [Module inventory](#module-inventory-and-placement-rules) |
+| Want to reuse vLLM forward code, but tangled in paged KV / cudagraph / scheduling | [Call kernels only](#reproducing-the-forward-call-kernels-only-do-not-port-the-scheduler) |
+| Weight mapping shapes are right, output silently degrades | [Mapping checks values and semantics](#43-mapping-checks-cover-values-and-semantics-not-only-shape) |
+| Inference kernel has no backward; should we write one | [Three-case decision](backward-validation.md#three-cases) |
+| Wrote a VJP; how to prove it is right | [Module-level comparison steps](backward-validation.md#comparison-steps) |
+| Unit tests pass but real training fails / step 0 occasionally not bitwise | [Two test-infrastructure false negatives](backward-validation.md#two-test-infrastructure-false-negatives); [BI kernels](bi-kernels.md) |
+| Changes after modifying packing or CP/TP/EP; wrong only on long sequences | [Layout and length](#distributed-layout-length-boundaries-and-training-side-acceptance) |
+| `ppo_kl` non-zero after rollout switches parallel layout (e.g. DP+EP to TP1 per GPU) | [Bitwise identity after changing the parallel layout](#bitwise-identity-after-changing-the-parallel-layout) |

+| Which kernel an operator uses in BI mode and its cost | [BI kernels](bi-kernels.md) |
+
+## Key rules
+
+1. Semantics follow the vLLM implementation and the checkpoint.
+2. Before starting, list for every module whether its inference kernel has a backward.
+3. Call kernels only; do not port the scheduler. mLite (BI=1): FP32 logprob raw bytes vs vLLM-captured trajectories, target 0 diff. FSDP2 / MCore (BI=0): no 0-diff target; judge each side against an independent reference, then look at precision.
+4. Mapping checks cover values and semantics, not only shape; fused parameters are overwritten whole.
+5. The precision contract lives in the model. Under VERL's bf16 autocast, casting only the inputs of matmul-type operators (including `F.linear` and `einsum` decomposed into bmm) does not stop the downgrade. +7. Reuse model-agnostic operators: mLite `primitive/modules` and `ops` first, then MCore/TE/mamba_ssm; only then is it new code.

+## Module inventory and placement rules
+
+List per module: inference kernel, same-math training implementation, quantization rounding, discrete selection, backward. Then pick the route and each module's place in the code tree. This catches missing backwards before they cost weeks.
+
+Training support means an implementation we maintain that backpropagates correctly. Config registration, same-family fallback, the vLLM inference implementation and third-party implementations in the image (newer Transformers modeling, NeMo AutoModel) do not count. Write it per [Reproducing the forward](#reproducing-the-forward-call-kernels-only-do-not-port-the-scheduler) into real source files and verify by loading through the actual loader in a new process. A REPL-only implementation or runtime monkeypatch is not evidence.
+

+### 3. Placement rules
+
+#### 3.1 mLite (Megatron `experimental/lite/megatron/lite`)
+
+Read `experimental/lite/docs/porting.md` and `architecture.md` first. Three layers: `runtime` (lifecycle, training-step orchestration), `model` (registration + model-specific build/load/export protocol), `primitive` (reusable: parallel state, TP layers, checkpoint conversion, MoE utilities, optimizer wrappers). The runtime knows no model details: it gets the protocol from the registry, builds a typed config, and lets the protocol build the model.
+
+| Rule | Content |
+| --- | --- |
+| The model directory holds only four things | `model/<name>/`: config, checkpoint mapping (WeightSpec), assembly, protocol. Impl name `lite` (`<name>/lite/`) |
+| Modules go into primitive | norm / linear / router / experts / dispatcher / attention -> `primitive/modules`; generic VJP bridge -> `primitive/ops`; quantization encoding -> `primitive/quantization`; PP splitting, thd, CP -> `primitive/parallel`; HF read/write via `primitive/ckpt/hf_weights` (`SafeTensorReader`, `load_hf_weights`, `export_hf_weights`) |
+| Model-specific math still goes into primitive and is registered | e.g. Mamba2 bridge, FP8-KV attention -> `primitive/modules/<x>.py`; no same-named `primitive/` under the model directory |
+| No file for reused backward | Reusing TE / mamba_ssm backward means no `backward.py`; glue goes in the module file |
+| Dependencies are one-directional | `model/` imports `primitive/`, never the reverse; top-level checkpoint/quantization does not import the impl subtree |
+| Layering guards must be registered | Add the model to `tests/unit/runtime/test_layering_contracts.py` or the guard does not apply |
+| No hybrid architecture packages | porting.md: "Keep these out of the first PR: Hybrid model implementation packages"; hybrid (Mamba + attention + MoE) modules are split into primitive |
+| State third-party kernel dependencies | Document hard dependencies on vllm, flashinfer private APIs, mamba_ssm, causal_conv1d, and the `init_batch_invariance()` call in build_model |

+#### 3.3 FSDP2 (VERL's HF interface path)
+
+- Write a PyTorch model to vLLM semantics in the Transformers `PreTrainedModel` / config interface so the VERL loader, PEFT and HF save/load use it directly. "HF" is only the interface and weight format.
+- Delivery: the model goes into the verl trunk, registered to the Auto classes (`AutoConfig` / `AutoModelForCausalLM`, etc.), and ships with the recipe as one verl PR ([Code and delivery §8](../practices/code-and-delivery.md#verl-a-thin-recipe-not-a-second-training-framework)). The verl FSDP extension guide's advice against copying modeling into `verl/models` targets models already in transformers. Register at the current checkout's FSDP load chain (`get_hf_auto_model_class` -> `from_pretrained`).
+- Develop and deliver from the same verl source and registration entry. Do not modify the checkpoint's `config.json` / `auto_map` (the low-precision checkpoint is the single source of truth) or enable `trust_remote_code`. The load log must show our registered class was used.
+- VERL's automodel engine (`automodel_actor`) uses NeMo AutoModel and is not this route; routes are distinguished by forward source, not by FSDP2 sharding.
+- Under bf16 autocast, FP32 computations (position-encoding angles, router logits and bias, norm statistics, following vLLM) disable autocast inside the module and set the dtype.
+- Backward prefers autograd; add operators next to the model file only when a backward is missing or too slow (the 160-line PyTorch Mamba scan reference).
+- Common pitfalls: `--system-site-packages` ABI, the actual `use_remove_padding`, PEFT targets not going through nn.Linear.
+- Under EP4 + FSDP2, all ranks' DCP expert shards share key and offset, so restore reads another rank's experts; the key must carry the EP rank ([checkpoint guide](checkpoint-resume.md)).

+## Reproducing the forward: call kernels only, do not port the scheduler
+
+The first deliverable after the inventory is a training forward with vLLM's math. Logprob measurement basis and R3 route replay: [workflow](../workflow/README.md), [rollout engine](rollout-engine.md).
+
+### 1. First separate the responsibilities of the model implementation and the training framework
+
+A training framework (FSDP2, MCore, mLite runtime) shards a trainable model; it does not make an inference-only kernel differentiable or write the model. Write a minimal PyTorch model for the current loader interface covering the config, checkpoint loading, forward, gradients and save interface actually used; full Transformers integration, generation and all parallelism are not needed first. The semantic basis is vLLM and the checkpoint, not a third-party implementation in the image.
+
+| Capability | What the training route still has to do | What in inference / Megatron is not copied |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Model math | Real semantics of attention/SSM, norm, position encoding, routing, residuals, special embeddings | vLLM paged KV, decode scheduling, cudagraph management; MCore provider/ModuleSpec wiring |
+| Backpropagation | Input gradients of every training-path operator; trained-parameter gradients; recompute correctness ([Backward validation](backward-validation.md)) | TP/SP/CP-specific collectives and gradient reduction |
+| Weights | Names, axes, fused order, expert IDs, sharing, derived state | HF<->Megatron shard layout, PP export protocol |
+| LoRA | Target coverage, A/B direction and scaling, non-zero adapter taking effect | Parallel linear wrapper, TP adapter aggregation |
+| Memory | Initialization peak, large frozen table residency, save/export peak | Megatron memory saver, PP scheduling |
+
+dtype, dequantization, QAT and update format: [precision guide](precision-quant.md). Here each module states its input/output precision and differentiable boundary.
+
+### 2. How to wire kernel-only calls
+
+Each layer's forward runs once: call the vLLM kernel for the visible output, bitwise identical to inference, and save what the backward needs; see [backward wiring](backward-validation.md#how-to-wire-it-forward-once-backward-uses-what-the-forward-saved). Borrow only the kernel, no vLLM runtime object:
+
+- No KV paging, decode scheduling or CUDA Graph management. Training runs a full-sequence teacher-forced forward; packing passes boundaries via thd/cu_seqlens.
+- Reuse order: model-agnostic differentiable operators -> concise PyTorch reference to vLLM semantics -> ready-made operators with backward -> custom autograd/kernel only if necessary. This order only says where to look first; the training-step cost of each choice is checked at C6 against the C1 budget, not deferred to C10.
+- Handle discrete top-k / index selection apart from the selected differentiable tensors. What is trained, frozen or given an auxiliary loss follows the model definition; do not detach to get it running or add router/indexer objectives.
+- vLLM layer modules used directly (FusedMoE, ModelOpt linear) need `get_tp/ep_group`, so the training process creates vLLM process groups (Nemotron does; DS4's own modules do not).
+- Take the same branch as inference: reproduce the quantization config, attention backend and BI-switch kernel selection, or the comparison is against a different path. Tests use the production `CompilationConfig(custom_ops=...)` ([the two false negatives](backward-validation.md#two-test-infrastructure-false-negatives)).
+
+"The same kernel" still has pitfalls (Nemotron 7-layer localization):
+
+1. Direct and compiled paths of the same gated RMS kernel differ; calling it through an opaque custom-op boundary removed the difference.
+2. A differing reduction block was wrongly blamed alone; the same captured kernel showed both blocks match.
+3. The last 4.768e-7 logprob difference came from the HF forward calling `.float()` after lm_head; keeping the real BF16 head output and sharing the scoring fixed it. This is not truncating an FP32 projection to BF16 to manufacture equality.
+
+### 3. Read the inference implementation along the full support chain
+
+Order: model file (layer types and order, residual and norm positions, position encoding, attention visibility, router/indexer, special embeddings) -> each layer's actual kernel and quantization variant -> attention backend and KV dtype -> weight loader (name mapping, fused order, derived scale) -> BI-switch branches. Confirm the parameter/buffer list from the same checkpoint/config.
+
+Sizes sharing one implementation need no separate port. For ordinary dense models, look for a reusable generic skeleton first; we still write the model. Multimodal is validated per task; diffusion is out of scope.

+### 4. The minimal implementation that really has to be filled in
+
+#### 4.1 Reproduce the math
+
+Confirm from the checkpoint/config and inference code: layer types and order, parameters/buffers, residual and norm positions, position encoding, attention visibility, router/indexer, special embeddings. Model-specific math (`sqrt(softplus)` scoring, SwiGLU with clamp, mHC Sinkhorn, ReLU² experts) is in no library; write it from the inference source, not the paper.
+
+#### 4.2 A frozen base still has to propagate input gradients
+
+```python
+W.requires_grad_(False)
+y = linear(x, W) + scale * B(A(x))  # no gradient for W, but still propagate to x
+loss(y).backward()
+```
+
+Wrapping a frozen block in `no_grad()` cuts LoRA gradients of earlier layers; only a frozen table lookup needing no input/parameter derivative is exempt. With initial B=0 a zero gradient for A can be normal; test with a non-zero adapter or a real step. A finite loss does not prove backward.
+
+<a id="33-shape"></a>
+
+#### 4.3 Mapping checks cover values and semantics, not only shape
+
+Per weight class: source name -> training name -> serving name, axis transforms, sharing. Focus on fused QKV, gate/up order, expert numbering, extra norm/bias, tie weights, non-persistent buffers, derived state (FP8 KV scale, NVFP4 alpha). Every missing/extra item needs a reason; quantization-derived items follow the precision guide and need not be byte-identical to the low-precision source. FSDP needs no HF<->Megatron bridge but may need checkpoint->training and export mappings.
+
+#### 4.4 Packing boundaries for Mamba / stateful modules
+
+Every stateful operator (conv1d, SSM scan, recurrence, PLE shift) must consume sequence boundaries; a correct attention mask proves nothing about them. Incidents:
+
+- verl via Megatron-Bridge did not pass boundaries to Mamba; sequence states mixed and logprob was silently wrong, visible only as a larger mismatch.
+- Qwen3.8 Flash-Next's PLE shift made the second sample reference the first sample's last token.
+
+Check: unequal-length A/B run separately and merged; sentinel-initialized outputs to catch missed writes. In mLite, derive boundary metadata from `PackedSeqParams`/`ThdPackMeta`, not a separate `SSMMeta`. See also [Long-sequence boundary points](#long-sequence-boundary-points).
+
+#### 4.5 Recompute and small-model trimming
+
+With activation checkpointing on, verify recompute reads the same state and gives reasonable gradients. Trim to the smallest layer set covering every non-equivalent path and its dependencies, usually 4-6 layers; keep mixed attention, cross-layer sharing and layer-specific table lookups. Record kept layer indices and the config transform; a slice proves only covered paths, not full-model mismatch or score gain.
+
+### 5. How to prove it computes the same math
+
+Feed the training forward vLLM-captured trajectories (fixed tokens, weight version, position, mask, routing); never compare probability summaries or argmax. mLite (BI=1): FP32 logprob raw bytes, target 0 diff. FSDP2 / MCore (BI=0): judge each side against an independent reference, then check the remaining difference comes only from precision rules.
+
+- Same policy weights. Differing dtypes are a contract mismatch; do not convert to fake bitwise.
+- Reference artifact (Nemotron): frozen trainer image, full actor, 2048 tokens, FP32 0 diff; five real updates, 883,998 tokens of identical FP32 logprob.
+- Old-logprob recomputation and the grad-enabled forward are two paths; evidence for each ([dual-path contract](../workflow/validation.md#old-logprob-and-training-forward-dual-path-contract)).
+- Find the first divergence per [debugging](debugging-mismatch.md): per-module dump, single-request prefill, then the operator.

+## Distributed layout, length boundaries and training-side acceptance
+
+Record trainer and rollout topologies separately. TP/CP/EP, padding, packing and collectives change data mapping and reduction paths; long sequences hit untested boundaries; forward 0 diff does not vouch for gradients or the optimizer.
+
+### Compute resources first, then request them
+
+Write trainer and rollout process groups separately. At four GPUs per node, an inference DP8/EP8 group spans two nodes; two DP4/EP4 replicas are not one EP8 group and skip cross-node EP communication. The runtime decides grouping.
+
+If dense DP excludes CP: `W = TP × PP × CP × DP`. Expert side: verify `W = ETP × EP × PP × EDP` and the CP mapping separately. **Do not multiply EP into the dense world again.** W=8, TP1/PP2/CP2 gives DP=2; a log calling DP×CP "DP" shows 4. Clarify naming and members; do not change GPU count to match a config string.
+
+GPU memory follows the layout. With PP1 each rank holds all layers' activations, linear in sequence length. Per-route EP backward state stored for other ranks' slots grows by the average ranks per token; store only own routes. Rollout `gpu_memory_utilization` is set from what training still holds during rollout, per training mode, in the recipe ([Memory budget 02 §5](checkpoint-resume.md#5-gpu-memory-set-gpu_memory_utilization-per-mode-when-training-and-rollout-are-colocated)).
+
+### Packing and CP
+
+For the target UID reconstruct global request `[seq_start, seq_end)`, rank range `[rank_start, rank_end)`, local rows, cu_seqlens, positions, all compression/reordering mappings.
+
+The intersection `[max(seq_start, rank_start), min(seq_end, rank_end))` contributes rows only when start < end. The overlap window must not give a disjoint request this rank's output. Host cumulative boundaries equal the rows the device compactor produces.
+
+Cover: before/after/at the boundary, empty intersection, cross-rank, compression-ratio and tile remainders. Window constant 8: check 1…7, not only multiples. Start from a hand-computable counterexample, then enumerate nearby legal configs.
+
+Passing `cu_seqlens` does not mean a fallback consumes it ([§4.4](#44-packing-boundaries-for-mamba--stateful-modules)).
+
+### EP and collectives
+
+Record expert mapping, tokens per rank, padding capacity, route order, shared/routed combine, quantization scales. Empty ranks may still join collectives; partially written reused buffers leave stale data. Use different sentinels per side; zero-filling both gives a false green.
+
+Pinning NCCL algorithm/channels may remove reduction differences on one stack and cut throughput significantly; verify it per topology, not as a universal env list, before relaxing config or building a deterministic collective.
+
+MCore dev's grad-ready assertion takes first-batch hook counts as golden and errors on a different count. Short-sequence micro-batches can make counts data-dependent (Nemotron r10 at step 2; r12 did not reproduce). With dp×cp=1 and expert_dp=1, `overlap_grad_reduce` off avoids it without changing values; root cause unknown. With EP4 + dist_opt and dp>1, multi-micro-batch reduction fires early (reported).
+
+### Bitwise identity after changing the parallel layout
+
+**Principle.** Floating-point addition is not associative. Layout sets reduction grouping, order and rounding: TP splits a matmul into per-rank partial sums; EP computes a token's top-k experts on different ranks and merges. Last-bit differences become different tokens after dozens of layers and sampling, so bitwise identity holds only for the verified layout; any TP/EP/DP change must be proven again.
+
+**Rules.**
+
+1. The reduction tree is part of the numerical contract: per level, accumulation dtype, order and rounding points. All legal rollout layouts and training walk the same tree.
+2. A degenerate layout (TP=1, EP=1) must simulate the tree: per-rank partial sums, same rounding, same merge order.
+3. After a layout change, compare per-token logprob raw bytes on fixed inputs before training. Non-zero `ppo_kl`/probs_diff is fixed, not avoided by reverting the layout.
+4. Locate: dump per layer, find the first differing layer, confirm its inputs (MoE: router logits too) are bitwise equal; the bug is that layer's reduction ([Fault localization](debugging-mismatch.md#bisect-and-first-divergence)).
+5. Measure the cost of simulating the order and report it apart from the layout gain.
+
+**Examples.**
+
+| Model | Layout change | Where the difference is | Fix and result |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Nemotron-H (W4A16 MoE, BI=1) | rollout from DP4EP4 per node to TP1 per GPU | EP4: per-rank FP32 sums rounded to BF16, merged in FP32 as `((s0+s1)+(s2+s3))+(s4+s5)`. EP1: six outputs summed sequentially in FP32, no intermediate rounding. Max logprob diff 0.4; greedy tokens diverge at positions 10–129 | Without EP, BI mode computes all experts in one launch and reduces in EP4 order (vLLM `661cde6833`, not in the image). Both layouts match training bitwise; `ppo_kl` 0 over 58 steps; multi-turn replay 404 s vs 485 s, reduction cost about 2.5% |
+| DeepSeek V4.1 | training TP=1, inference TP>1 | order of per-TP-rank partial sums | both sides use one fixed reduction tree, TP=1 included (`VLLM_TP_INVARIANT_LEAVES`) |
+

+
+Check streams, events, buffer owners and reuse timing. Passing with a global synchronize only proves a timing issue and is not the fix; find the missing dependency and accept on the same path.

+### Long-sequence boundary points

+| Boundary | Fact | How to test |

+| KV page | training attention replicates vLLM's KV page size; page boundaries are numerical boundaries | sparse dY across the page boundary |
+| Fixed split attention | fixed split count and keys per split; the resulting `MAX_SEQ_LEN` is an invariance bound, not a performance knob | above: error, not silent truncation; below: two real lengths × random/zero/sparse dY |

+# Evidence and experiment rules
+
+Rules for what counts as evidence, how experiments are designed and recorded, and when old evidence stops holding. Mechanisms live in the guides.
+
+## 1. Evidence labels
+
+PASS / FAIL / INVALID (did not enter the target path) / VACUOUS (condition had zero hits) / SUPERSEDED / HISTORICAL. These label evidence, not lifecycle states. The tables in [validation.md](../workflow/validation.md) and the [report template](../workflow/report-template.md) have only `pass / fail / inconclusive / not run`. PASS→`pass`, FAIL→`fail`; INVALID and VACUOUS become `inconclusive` with the reason in the notes; SUPERSEDED and HISTORICAL stay out of the current table and live only in the [candidate evidence ledger](#6-candidate-evidence-ledger) and historical reports. One SUPERSEDED piece of evidence makes the gate it covered stale. A successful run, train-inference consistency and a held-out score gain are different conclusions and cannot substitute for each other.
+
+## 2. Evidence that must not be confused
+
+- Enabling `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is not cross-framework bitwise alignment; the same text is not the same logprob.
+- Zero difference in probability space, zero KL or identical printed numbers do not replace comparing valid logprobs in the original dtype.
+- Replaying fixed inputs is a localization tool; statistics from old trajectories are not an unbiased KL under the current policy.
+- The same function name, generated code or environment variables do not prove the same actual kernel, launch config and shared libraries.
+- Output replacement, forced routing, disabling Graph and bypassing bad packing are valid causal experiments if you state what they change.
+- Similar quality scores are not identical per-problem results; same-problem quality, bitwise logprob and 8K/1K performance are accounted separately. When the acceptance script fails, check the producer receipt first; do not resample or declare a pass automatically.
+- Verify quantization rules on the deployed bytes, not dequantized weights ([precision pitfall P2](../guides/precision-quant.md#p2-verifying-a-rule-with-dequantized-weights-gives-a-false-positive)). QAT/low-precision training only narrows the weight gap; 0 diff comes only from training calling the same kernel as inference; see [How much QAT can shrink the mismatch](../guides/precision-quant.md#4-how-much-mismatch-qat-can-remove).
+- Do not manufacture a pass by changing tokens, weights, model geometry, precision or tolerance. If the comparison baseline really must change, start a new experiment and re-verify quality.
+- Do not carry DS4's EP/MoE config over to dense Qwen; do not manufacture a performance gain by weakening the BI=0 config, locally disguising BI as off, or removing existing correctness patches.
+- Source tests passing is not the final image passing. Development overlay results belong only to their experiment; the delivered image digest, installed source and build artifacts must match the acceptance object, and the evidence chain is rebuilt after repackaging.
+
+## 3. Inferences no longer carried forward
+
+Historical numbers and criteria stay with the run that produced them; a new task does not inherit a past run's model, dataset, topology, performance statistics method or pass status. Lessons from retracted or narrowed claims:
+
+- A number in a summary is not evidence: find the raw numerator and denominator for the same policy/workload/config, or retract the assertion.
+- Execution completion is not numerical acceptance: finished steps, a started job, an existing adapter file or finite nonzero gradients do not show the target class ran or the comparison passed. Record the instantiated class and its import source, and accept non-empty original-dtype token comparison, module VJP against an independent reference, actual update, shutdown and long-term stability separately.
+- Evidence does not transfer across candidates: a source pin, the same Docker tag, an earlier proxy, an experiment stack or a direct operator call does not prove the current candidate, image or compiled module dispatch. Verify branch, dirty patch, wheel, `.so`, dependencies and digest separately, and re-establish entry-gate evidence for the current candidate.
+- A fixed split count or a pass on one path does not cover other batches, prefill/decode, the first round after resume or cross-node communication; each needs its own evidence.
+- When an acceptance wrapper fails, find the failing layer before resampling or rerunning; a control-plane parsing error does not discard sealed numerical evidence.
+
+Each new case records only "contract → minimal counterexample → discriminating experiment → root cause/minimal fix → regression on the original reproducer → scope/source", with the small raw receipt for disputed numbers. Merge status, recommended dependency versions and best-performing config are volatile; look them up in the target repo.
+
+## 4. Experiment contract
+
+### Define the objects of equality first
+
+State the checkpoint/adapter/policy version, tokenizer and chat template, raw token IDs, position IDs, attention/response mask, padding/packing, and the logits processing on both training and inference sides.
+
+For response token `y[t]`, compare `log p(y[t] | prompt, y[:t])`. Make explicit the prediction position of the first response token, whether EOS counts, and the exclusion rules for truncation and padding. Do not align logits rows of different positions.
+
+Distinguish raw logits, raw logprobs, and logprobs after temperature/repetition penalty/top-k/top-p, and record which one the interface returns. The same seed does not guarantee the same scheduling or RNG consumption: freeze the tokens instead of resampling.
+
+### Record these goals separately
+
+| Goal | Valid evidence | Cannot infer |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Single-side repeatability | A/A with the same input and state | Consistency across batches or processes |
+| batch/layout invariance | Same semantic sample identical under different positions, neighbors and packing | Training and inference are the same |
+| prefill/decode parity | Two execution paths with the same forced tokens | backward or the training update is correct |
+| Cross-stack forward parity | Real training forward against a frozen rollout | Full-vocabulary logits match, if only sampled tokens are compared |
+| Effective training loop | Non-degenerate gradients, parameter change, post-update parity | Convergence or long-term stability |
+
